evidence.reason: The parser slices each NUL-delimited `git ls-files --stage -z` record correctly, but then applies `(.+)` without the `s` flag. JavaScript `.` excludes line terminators, so a tracked filename containing a newline or carriage return cannot match the regex, producing `entry === null` and throwing `terminal foreign index entry unsupported` even when that foreign path is unrelated to the attempted edit. Git emits such filenames verbatim under `-z`, so this is a real settlement-aborting defect. The smallest compatible repair is to match across line terminators, e.g. `([\s\S]+)$`, or parse the path from the first tab to the NUL boundary.
